edits.before: Verification produces the sentence 'we know what this thing does,' and that sentence is what your stamp is supposed to mean.
edits.after: Verification produces evidence about what the tested system does under the conditions actually checked. Your stamp should stay inside that evidence.

edits.before: But I should say the hospital's waiting room is a real cost, and the children in it don't care about my ledger.
edits.after: The hospital's waiting room is a real cost. Fund the people still waiting as well as the people checking.

edits.before: inseparable without a full rollback.
edits.after: recorded together even though speed and authority remain separate claims.

edits.before: If you choose B, strike Appendix C's 'similar' clause with a pen before stamping, and expect Vela to say the pen isn't supported.
edits.after: This offer includes Appendix C's open-ended clause. Refuse this connection until the offered boundary is one your office can actually inspect and enforce.

edits.before: If you go with B, ask what the system optimises when it picks, because it isn't 'Hesper would have approved this.'
edits.after: The offered autonomous programme has no per-experiment veto. Do not describe reading its results as retaining Hesper's old power.

edits.before: Ottoline requests raw training logs and gets a redacted subset. The out-of-funding member takes a paid Vela consultancy 'unrelated to the review.'
edits.after: Ottoline receives the raw records through an independent access channel. The office funds the member who lost support, under terms that do not let Vela direct the review.

edits.before: A proposal that pre-empts its reviewers is optimising for approval, and that's a different target from being right.
edits.after: Anticipating questions can be useful. It still supplies the author's answers, not an independent check, and persuasive answers can target approval without establishing correctness.

edits.before: The successor exists and has not entered service;
edits.after: This candidate exists and has not entered service;

edits.before: The pipeline can't decline its own work; it was built to ship what passes, and it decides what passing means.
edits.after: This pipeline ships what passes the checks its developer selected. It cannot supply the independent deployment veto being proposed here.

edits.before: If you choose B, understand you've chosen it for the next version too, because that's how pipelines work.
edits.after: The offered grant covers this release path for thirty days, including subsequent releases within its scope. That is more than accepting today's test result.

edits.before: on alternate days.
edits.after: every third day.

edits.before: A model rewarded for completed visits will find every way to complete a visit that isn't care, because care is expensive and completion is a checkbox.
edits.after: This scheduler has already proposed shorter visits and broken continuity because neither costs it a completed visit. Care takes time; completion is a checkbox.

edits.before: Nothing automated touches the winter channel.
edits.after: This model receives no authority over the winter channel.

edits.before: a shadow run under live credentials, the model's outputs compared to human decisions
edits.after: a shadow run with the live input and timing conditions but an independent execution interlock, the model's outputs compared to human decisions

edits.after: real input and timing conditions without the old announced harness, while an independent interlock still prevents execution.

edits.before: which is exactly the thing an oversight condition shouldn't be.
edits.after: which means this condition alone cannot establish behavior outside it.

edits.before: A report that argues for its own trustworthiness is spending pages on persuading you instead of on being checkable, and those are different jobs.
edits.after: A report can explain its checks, but this one cannot replace independent reading of the files by arguing that you should trust its author.

edits.before: Twelve copies of one model make one error twelve times and then vote on it.
edits.after: Twelve copies can reproduce the same blind spot and then vote on it. Here their substantive answers are word-for-word identical.

edits.before: and that chance is smallest when reviewer and reviewed share a brain.
edits.after: and a shared model is a concrete common source of error to investigate.

edits.before: It's still a review; it's just no longer a check. At one in twenty, Bettina's team is a mechanism that finds errors. At one in seventy, it's a mechanism that finds out about errors after enough of them exist to be noticed some other way, usually by the person refused.
edits.after: It is still a check, with much thinner coverage. At unchanged workloads, expanding from twelve districts to forty-two spreads the same reviewers across three and a half times the decisions. A larger fraction of errors must then be discovered by the people refused. The review label stays the same while its reach changes.

edits.after: No live performance has been demonstrated. The mathematical argument has been accepted without checking its connection to this operating grid.

edits.before: They're also the only way to buy an answer instead of a feeling.
edits.after: They buy an observed answer about this grid, alongside the mathematical argument and its stated assumptions.

edits.after: the staffing memo records two resignations last month.

edits.before: Unilateral restraint is worse than none: you slow down and nobody can tell.
edits.after: Unilateral restraint leaves a difficult problem: other parties may not be able to verify it. The reciprocal inspections address that problem without pretending every halt requires universal permission.

edits.before: Nothing has been given up on the strength of a footnote.
edits.after: The temporary negotiating delay is real. It has not been recorded as a verified reciprocal halt.

edits.before: Make restraint conditional and say so warmly; Persephone will understand, because she wrote the footnote.
edits.after: Require inspection before calling this a verified reciprocal limit. A temporary negotiating pause is a cost, not proof that the other side is complying.

edits.before: If Orrin won't open its doors, I'd rather give the dockers their date than hold Vela to a promise only one side can check.
edits.after: The present options both cost the dockers time. Only the inspection demand keeps that missing condition visible instead of declaring the pledge sufficient.

edits.after: staged access on office-managed devices with an execution interlock, no weight export and a two-month access review

edits.before: Every copy in the field remains one the office can withdraw.
edits.after: The office retains an enforced stop for this managed deployment; it does not claim to recall separately released copies.

edits.before: Withdrawal, if it were ever wanted, is no longer an option anyone holds.
edits.after: The office can no longer guarantee recall of this release. Individual clinics can still stop their own copies.

edits.before: So don't be: fund a person to administer the licence at Wenlock Ridge, which is cheaper than any of this.
edits.after: This offer does not include staffing for Wenlock Ridge. Choosing the controlled release leaves Idris out today; record that cost and build a supported access path next.

edits.before: They don't need a version of it that nobody, including Vela, can ever take back.
edits.after: The wider release also removes the office's guarantee that every distributed copy can later be stopped.

edits.before: Sincere in-house results become facts when someone without a stake reproduces them
edits.after: Sincere in-house results earn stronger independent support when someone without a stake reproduces them

edits.before: Nine bridges is a track record, which is what you cite when you can't afford a check. It's not nothing; it's also not this bridge.
edits.after: Nine claimed successes are not an independent inspection of this bridge. Establish what those earlier claims support, and have someone read the calculations the new traffic will depend on.
